extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners/staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive MPEP guidance on when drawings are required for an application filing date, how to handle omitted drawing figures (OPAP notices, petitions, amendments), and requirements/process for specifying and changing correspondence addresses and power of attorney details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and the filing date for applications filed on or after December 18, 2013
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications other than design applications filed on or after December 18, 2013, drawings are not required in order to receive a filing date, but drawings should be submitted on filing if necessary for the understanding of the invention because no amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are necessary for understanding, they should be submitted with the initial filing since later amendments cannot add new matter. Applications filed with a specification (with or without drawings) on or after Dec. 18, 2013 are entitled to a filing date; nevertheless, submit drawings on filing when necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where drawings are usually not considered necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common categories in which drawings are usually unnecessary: (A) coated articles or products where invention resides solely in coating/impregnating a conventional sheet unless significant structural details are involved; (B) articles made from a particular material or composition unless significant structural details are involved; (C) laminated structures where invention involves only laminations of sheets/coatings unless significant details other than order of layers are involved; (D) articles/apparatus/systems whose sole distinguishing feature is the presence of a particular material (e.g., hydraulic system distinguished solely by a particular hydraulic fluid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories reflect USPTO practice treating such applications as not needing drawings for a filing date, but if significant structural/arrangement details are present drawings may still be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of applications filed without drawings when something can be construed as a written description
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application (filed prior to Dec. 18, 2013) or design application having at least one claim, or a provisional application having some disclosure, directed to subject matter usually not requiring drawings, filed without drawings but containing something that can be construed as a written description, will be processed (i.e., accorded a filing date) so long as there is something that can be construed as a written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Technology Center determines drawings are necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113, the filing date issue will be reconsidered and the application may be returned to OPAP for mailing of a 'Notice of Incomplete Application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) to establish entitlement to a filing date regarding drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) (with the petition fee) asserting that (A) the drawing(s) at issue was submitted, or (B) the drawing(s) is not necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 for a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by sufficient evidence (e.g., date-stamped postcard receipt) to establish entitlement to the requested filing date. For nonprovisional applications an alternative is to submit drawings and accept the date of such submission as the application filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of omitted drawings via amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b) when contained in a prior-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: If omitted drawing(s) were inadvertently omitted but the omitted portion is completely contained in a prior-filed foreign, provisional, nonprovisional, or international application for which priority/benefit is claimed, applicant may submit the omitted drawings by way of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendment must be identified as pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b) and must comply with 37 CFR 1.57(b) and 1.121. See MPEP § 217 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP review and Notice of Omitted Items when figures mentioned in the specification are missing
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP reviews application papers to determine whether all figures mentioned in the specification are present. If an application is missing drawing figures referred to in the specification but contains something that can be construed as a specification/written description, OPAP will send a notice (e.g., 'Notice of Omitted Item(s)') indicating the application has been accorded a filing date but is lacking some drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to nonprovisional applications filed prior to Dec. 18, 2013 or design applications; for applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (c) on/after Dec. 18, 2013, OPAP will send a 'Notice of Omitted Items' if drawings are lacking even if a specification is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant options after OPAP notice regarding missing drawing figures (establish prior receipt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following an OPAP notice about missing drawing figures, applicant may (A) promptly establish prior receipt by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) within two months from the OPAP notice date, with evidence of deposit; the petition fee will be refunded if the drawing(s) were in fact received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136. The petition must include evidence (e.g., a date-stamped receipt) to support the allegation that drawings were received with the original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant option to submit omitted drawings and request later filing date (petition under 37 CFR 1.182)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an OPAP notice, applicant may submit omitted drawing(s) in a nonprovisional application and, within two months, file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with the petition fee) requesting that the date of submission of the omitted drawing(s) be treated as the application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012, the omitted drawings must be accompanied by an oath/declaration in compliance with pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.64 referring to the drawings. The two-month period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant option to accept the application as deposited by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may accept the application as deposited by filing an amendment that either (1) includes replacement drawing sheets to renumber figures consecutively and a substitute specification canceling references to omitted drawings and correcting references (without adding new matter), or (2) files an amendment to add the missing figure(s) by relying on incorporation by reference under 37 CFR 1.57(b) or other portions of the original disclosure, without adding new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121(d), 1.121(b)(3), and 1.125 as applicable, and cannot add subject matter (see 35 U.S.C. 132(a)). If properly done, the application will maintain the original filing date (date of deposit). The specification must be amended to cancel references to omitted drawings and correct reference numerals shown only in omitted drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and alternatives when submitting omitted drawings (new application alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of omitted drawings in a nonprovisional application and acceptance of the date of such submission as the filing date is tantamount to filing a new application. Applicants should consider filing a new application as an alternative to filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.182; for provisional applications, the USPTO will not grant 1.182 petitions to accept omitted drawings and accord the later date, so applicants should file a new provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a new application can be a cost-effective alternative, especially where the original nonprovisional was deposited without filing fees or where the provisional filing fee is relatively low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely reply to OPAP notice leads to abandonment (nonprovisional) or automatic abandonment (provisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for which an OPAP notice regarding omitted items has been mailed will be retained in OPAP to await a reply. Failure to timely reply to the OPAP notice in a nonprovisional application will result in abandonment. For provisional applications where applicant accepts the application as deposited by failing to file a petition, if the provisional is complete under 37 CFR 1.51(c) it will be held in IFW and automatically abandoned at the end of its pendency period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response to OPAP notices is required to avoid abandonment; two-month periods and extendability rules apply per the specific option invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction required when specification refers to a figure number but drawings use number-letter labels
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings include figures labeled with a number-letter combination (e.g., Fig. 1A, 1B, 1C) but the specification refers to the figure by the base number only (e.g., 'Figure 1'), this is an error in the specification which must be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction will be required (e.g., amend specification to match drawing labels or renumber drawings) so that references correspond to actual drawing figure labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review steps when forwarded application lacks drawing figures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application forwarded for examination was filed without all drawing figures referred to in the specification and OPAP notice has not been mailed, the examiner should review the application to determine whether the application is entitled to a filing date (for applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) prior to Dec. 18, 2013 or design applications). If entitled, the examiner should notify applicant of the omission in the next Office action and require applicant to accept one of the enumerated options (accept as filed; file omitted drawings + petition 1.182; or file petition 1.53(e) alleging drawings were deposited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines the application is not entitled to a filing date because no drawing figure is present and a drawing is necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113, the examiner should forward the application to OPAP for mailing of a 'Notice of Incomplete Application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when accepting application as filed though missing drawings (examiner response)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant chooses to accept the application as filed without all drawing figures, applicant must submit: (1) an amendment to the specification canceling all references to the omitted drawing figures including any reference numerals shown only in the omitted drawing figures; (2) an amendment with replacement drawing sheets renumbering drawing figures consecutively in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d); and (3) a further amendment to the specification correcting references to correspond with relabeled drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments should be submitted in response to the Office action; the amendments must not add new matter and must comply with the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior-filed application to supply inadvertently omitted drawing portions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the omitted drawings (or portions) were inadvertently omitted but are completely contained in a prior-filed foreign/provisional/nonprovisional/international application for which a priority/benefit claim exists, applicant may submit an amendment to include the inadvertently omitted portion pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must be identified as pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b) and must comply with 37 CFR 1.57(b) and 1.121. The application will maintain the original filing date and the original disclosure will include only those papers present on the original date of deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The attorney's or agent's full mailing address (including ZIP code) must be given in every power of attorney. Telephone and fax numbers of the attorney or agent should also be included to facilitate prompt delivery of communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 402.02(a) for detailed information and relevant forms pertaining to appointment of a power of attorney in applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012 and § 402.02(b) for applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to specify a correspondence address in an application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must specify a correspondence address to which the Office will send notices, letters, and other communications relating to an application. The correspondence address must be set forth in either an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with the application filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no correspondence address is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first-named inventor as the correspondence address. For electronic filings, an electronic acknowledgment will be sent to the submitter but a correspondence address must still be specified. The Office will generally not engage in double correspondence and will select one address if multiple are provided (may prefer the address associated with a Customer Number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules and guidance for changing correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office should be promptly notified of any change in correspondence address. The change should be provided in a manner that clearly calls attention to the fact that an address change is being made; mere inclusion of a different address in a paper filed for another purpose, without mention that an address change is being made, will not ordinarily be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.33(a) and related paragraphs specify who may change the correspondence address (e.g., patent practitioner of record, applicants per 1.42, or others in specified circumstances). If more than one correspondence address is specified the Office will select one, and the hierarchy in 37 CFR 1.76(d) governs inconsistencies. A change of address filed in an application or patent does not change the address for a patent practitioner in the roster under 37 CFR 11.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifics re correspondence address when using prior application papers in a continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application papers from a prior application are used in a continuing application and the correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, an application data sheet or separate paper identifying the correspondence address to be used for the continuing application must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not submitted, the Office may not recognize the change of correspondence address effected during prosecution of the prior application and correspondence may be mailed to the previously designated address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing correspondence address after patent issues by a practitioner acting in representative capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent practitioner acting in a representative capacity whose correspondence address is the correspondence address of record in an application may change the correspondence address after the patent has issued, provided the change is accompanied by a statement that notice has been given to the patentee or owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.33(g) provides this mechanism for practitioners acting in a representative capacity, but it does not authorize practitioners acting under 37 CFR 1.34 to change the correspondence address in an application.
